propositions: Pure single-pass evidence-prepack verification yields false-positive rejections when the prepack is imperfect; a filter+fallback design prevents false-positive rejection by construction by allowing the filter to only PASS or ABSTAIN, never reject.

The prepack builder deterministically assembles per-AC evidence (grep-at-ref symbols/paths, file impacts, referencing commits, test listings) capped at 6KB per AC, with thin packs for missing evidence and no synthesis.

Filter coverage is bimodal by AC style: ACs naming greppable artifacts (tests, symbols, files) achieve high pass rates from static packs; ACs asserting runtime outcomes or store-side artifacts rationally abstain.

Filter+fallback achieves -26% overall tokens and -46% on real all-met tickets vs pure-agentic, with the filter's own cost negligible (~0.4%), while maintaining zero false-positive passes on adversarial unmet ACs.

The existing criteria-reduction seam (AC-block rewrite at ticket load via monkeypatch of show_ticket) narrows the agentic step budget automatically, providing the narrowing mechanism without schema changes.

Agentic verifier variance dominates small deltas and the filter introduces context-sensitivity in judgment stability, requiring variance-aware cost interpretation and telemetry per AC style to determine filter applicability.
